title: Orchestrate variable hue bridges and radius constraints for inline widgets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Compact inline components (chips, tags, inline buttons, table-action pills) look inconsistent across the product due to ad-hoc color ramps and mixed radius rules. Small sizes lose perceived contrast and button affordance when shadows are too subtle or radii are mismatched. Goal: produce a constrained, accessible token subset and migration plan that defines variable hue bridges (semantic derivations for accents/interactive states), a proportional radius system for inline widget sizes, and a micro-elevation/shadow recipe tuned for small surfaces. Deliverables: token spec (names + fallback mapping), updated Figma styles, migration script for token renames, engineering acceptance tests and a design QA checklist. Rationale: harmonizing these primitives reduces visual noise, improves tap/scan affordance on compact controls, and simplifies runtime token selection (fewer special-case overrides in components).
acceptance_criteria: A token spec doc published to Confluence with explicit color derivation rules for primary/secondary/neutral accents and hover/pressed/disabled states
Figma library updated with compact-size styles (xs, s) that reference the new tokens and include margin/radius/shadow presets
Engineering has a migration mapping (old_token -> new_token) and a runbook for a phased rollout with feature-flagged rollout for major packages
Design QA checklist validated on three representative screens: Settings table, Compact chat threads, and Inline tag lists — screenshots attached
Automated visual regression tests added to the storybook snapshot suite for xs and s variants of Button, Tag, and Pill components
comments: 2026-03-09 Maya Chen: Kickoff — synched with frontend leads (Ava & Rafael). Agreed to avoid introducing new semantic names unless they simplify runtime routing. Decided to prioritize accent continuity over introducing new neutral ramps for this cycle.

2026-03-10 Jordan Patel: First draft token spreadsheet uploaded to Drive (see attachments). Proposing 'hue-bridge' tokens that compute two anchor colors per accent: accent-anchorp and accent-anchorv (primary/variant). Need eng input on automation for runtime derivation.

2026-03-10 Rafael (FE): Reviewed spreadsheet — technical trade-off: runtime derivation increases shader/kcache complexity but reduces bundle size. Suggested shipping static derived tokens first, then move to derive-on-init in runtime-2.

2026-03-11 Design review (Luca, Priya): Approved radius scale: [4,6,8] px for xs/s/m inline widgets respectively. Requested a tighter shadow for xs to preserve separation without raising perceived elevation.
2026-03-12 Jordan Patel: Created GitHub PR draft for token rename map: github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/4283 (WIP). Added migration runbook outline.

2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Updated Figma frames to include before/after states for compact tables. Leaving open items: accessibility contrast checks for disabled states; follow-up: pair with accessibility engineer Week 11.
implementation_notes: Implementation approach: 1) Publish the token spec as read-only first and update Figma; 2) Ship static derived tokens in ui-tokens package (v3.0) with a deprecation map for old tokens; 3) Add storybook stories for xs/s variants and baseline visual snapshots; 4) After rollout, experiment with runtime derivation (ENG-1842) to reduce token duplication. Engineering tasks are split across two sprints. Performance implication: small increase in stylesheet size initially, mitigated by tree-shaking and later runtime derivation.
